aws_cli_cache.what: cli\cache holds temporary credentials from assumed IAM roles; sso\cache holds IAM Identity Center (SSO) access tokens.
aws_cli_cache.used_for: Lets the AWS CLI call AWS without signing in again. After deletion the CLI asks you to run 'aws sso login' or re-assume the role.
aws_cli_cache.risk: Signs you out of the AWS CLI/SDKs; scripts and scheduled jobs using SSO profiles fail until you sign in again.
aws_cli_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right. These are credential caches, not junk; the catalog label 'config' is also wrong (config is not in these paths). Keep .aws refused by delete_items.

aws_toolkit_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\AWStoolkit is the AWS Toolkit extension's data folder (settings, telemetry ids, possibly SSO/session state).
aws_toolkit_cache.used_for: Used by the VS Code AWS Toolkit; removing it resets the extension.
aws_toolkit_cache.risk: May sign you out of AWS connections and reset extension settings.
aws_toolkit_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

box_cache.what: Box Drive's local cache of files you opened, moved or marked for offline use, plus Box Drive logs.
box_cache.used_for: Box keeps a copy so files open quickly and offline. Cached files are downloaded again from Box when next opened; logs are diagnostics only.
box_cache.risk: If Box Drive has changes not yet uploaded, the only copy may be in this cache and could be lost. Offline-marked files must re-download.
box_cache.before_cleaning: Quit Box Drive completely and make sure it shows no pending uploads
box_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog says 'safe'. The cache folder can hold not-yet-uploaded edits, so it should be 'caution' (logs alone are safe).

cloudflare_warp_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Cloudflare is the WARP client's per-user data folder (settings, registration).
cloudflare_warp_cache.used_for: Used by the WARP client; deleting it can force re-registration.
cloudflare_warp_cache.risk: Possible loss of WARP/Zero Trust enrollment and settings.
cloudflare_warp_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

cyberghost_cache.what: CyberGhost's API response cache plus the Cache / Code Cache / GPUCache subfolders of its WebView2 interface profile.
cyberghost_cache.used_for: API cache is refetched; the WebView2 caches are rebuilt on next start.
cyberghost_cache.risk: None known; the profile's Login Data and VPN tokens are NOT targeted (correctly).
cyberghost_cache.catalog_concern: Consistent with CLAUDE.md: BrowserCache is a whole WebView2 profile, so only its Cache subfolders are listed - keep it that way.

dropbox_cache.what: Dropbox's documented cache is a hidden '.dropbox.cache' folder inside your Dropbox folder. The catalog's AppData 'cache' and 'logs' subfolders are not documented; logs are diagnostics.
dropbox_cache.used_for: Dropbox's cache holds temporary files for uploads/downloads and is auto-cleared every three days.
dropbox_cache.risk: Low for logs. The AppData Dropbox folders around these paths hold the instance databases and sign-in; they must never be targeted.
dropbox_cache.catalog_concern: Paths do not match Dropbox's documented cache (%HOMEPATH%\Dropbox\.dropbox.cache), so this likely finds little. Description mentions 'cache.db' - never widen to the parent AppData\Dropbox folders (instance1 DBs, sign-in).

expressvpn_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A folder of ExpressVPN diagnostic log files.
expressvpn_cache.used_for: Logs help support diagnose connection problems; new logs are written as the app runs.
expressvpn_cache.risk: Lose diagnostics for past connection problems.
expressvpn_cache.catalog_concern: Description mentions 'split-tunneling config cache' - the path is a logs folder; if it ever held config, deletion would reset split tunneling.

firebase_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\firebase can hold the Firebase CLI's sign-in tokens and emulator data.
firebase_cache.used_for: Firebase CLI state; deletion means 'firebase login' again and lost local emulator data.
firebase_cache.risk: Sign-out of Firebase CLI; loss of emulator exports.
firebase_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

google_drive_cache.what: Google Drive for desktop keeps its data under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\DriveFS: per-account content cache (including files waiting to upload) and Logs. A top-level 'Cache' subfolder is not documented.
google_drive_cache.used_for: The content cache makes streamed files open fast and holds files before upload. Logs are diagnostics, rebuilt as Drive runs.
google_drive_cache.risk: Google warns: files are moved into the cache before upload; clearing it before upload completes loses that file. Logs: lost diagnostics only.
google_drive_cache.before_cleaning: Quit Google Drive and confirm all uploads are finished
google_drive_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog says 'safe'. Logs are safe, but DriveFS cache data can contain unsynced uploads; never widen this to DriveFS or <account>\content_cache.

heroku_cli_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Heroku is the Heroku CLI's data folder (config, plugins, possibly auth).
heroku_cli_cache.used_for: Deleting it resets the CLI and its plugins.
heroku_cli_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

icloud_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A cache subfolder of iCloud for Windows.
icloud_cache.used_for: Presumably temporary data the iCloud client re-downloads as needed.
icloud_cache.risk: Unknown; iCloud may re-download data. iCloud Drive files themselves live elsewhere.
icloud_cache.catalog_concern: Undocumented path; the Microsoft Store version of iCloud keeps data under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages, so this may find nothing.

ipvanish_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\IPVanish is the client's whole data folder (settings, profiles, logs).
ipvanish_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

mega_cache.what: MEGA desktop app's logs (Local\Mega Limited\MEGAsync\logs) and temporary transfer files; the 'cache' under Roaming is not documented.
mega_cache.used_for: Logs are diagnostics; temp files are partial transfers the app restarts.
mega_cache.risk: An in-progress transfer may restart. The sync database in the same parent folder must not be touched (description wrongly says 'sync database').
mega_cache.before_cleaning: Quit MEGA and make sure no transfers are running
mega_cache.catalog_concern: Description says 'sync database' - the listed paths do not include it and must not: deleting MEGAsync's DB forces a full rescan or re-login.

mullvad_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Mullvad VPN is the GUI's data folder (settings, gui state).
mullvad_cache.used_for: Deletion resets the app's GUI settings.
mullvad_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

netlify_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\netlify holds the Netlify CLI config including its auth token.
netlify_cache.risk: Sign-out of Netlify CLI; lost linked-site config.
netlify_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

ngrok_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\ngrok can hold ngrok.yml with your authtoken.
ngrok_cache.used_for: Deletion removes the authtoken; tunnels fail until re-configured.
ngrok_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

nordvpn_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\NordVPN is the client's data folder; the second path is malformed (Roaming twice).
nordvpn_cache.risk: Lost settings and possibly the saved login.
nordvpn_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache. The path '%APPDATA%\Roaming\ClientConfig' is also malformed.

onedrive_cache.what: OneDrive sync client's diagnostic logs (Personal/Business subfolders, binary format). A 'cache' subfolder is not documented and does not exist here.
onedrive_cache.used_for: Logs are used only for troubleshooting; OneDrive writes new ones as it runs.
onedrive_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics for past sync problems. Files and settings are elsewhere (settings folder).
onedrive_cache.catalog_concern: Description ('known folder mask and sync conflict files') is wrong: these are logs. Overlaps 'onedrive_logs'. Never widen to OneDrive\settings (account and sync state).

onedrive_commercial_cache.what: Same folders as 'onedrive_cache': OneDrive sync client logs.
onedrive_commercial_cache.used_for: Diagnostics only; rewritten as OneDrive runs.
onedrive_commercial_cache.catalog_concern: Disabled only as a duplicate of 'onedrive_cache' - correct.

onedrive_full_cache.what: Same folders as 'onedrive_cache': OneDrive sync client logs.
onedrive_full_cache.used_for: Diagnostics only; rewritten as OneDrive runs.
onedrive_full_cache.catalog_concern: Disabled only as a duplicate of 'onedrive_cache' - correct.

onedrive_logs.what: The *.log files in OneDrive's logs folder.
onedrive_logs.used_for: Troubleshooting only; OneDrive writes new logs.
onedrive_logs.risk: Lost diagnostics for past sync problems.

openvpn_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\OpenVPN and OpenVPN Connect hold imported profiles (.ovpn, sometimes with keys/certificates), settings and logs.
openvpn_cache.risk: Lost VPN profiles, keys and settings.
openvpn_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

pcloud_cache.what: pCloud Drive's local cache (default %LOCALAPPDATA%\pCloud\Cache), temp files and logs.
pcloud_cache.used_for: pCloud caches files you open and stages uploads so they survive a dropped connection; cached copies are re-downloaded later.
pcloud_cache.risk: Uploads still pending may exist only in the cache and could be lost; files re-download on next open.
pcloud_cache.before_cleaning: Quit pCloud Drive after it shows everything uploaded
pcloud_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog says 'safe'. pCloud's cache stages uploads, so Cache should be 'caution'; temp and Logs are safe.

planetscale_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\planetscale holds the pscale CLI config and auth.
planetscale_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

sharepoint_cache.what: Office Document Cache (OfficeFileCache): Office's local copy of cloud documents, including edits not yet uploaded to OneDrive/SharePoint.
sharepoint_cache.used_for: Lets Office open and save cloud files quickly; Office's own 'Delete cached files' option is the supported way to clear it.
sharepoint_cache.risk: Unsaved/unuploaded changes to OneDrive or SharePoint documents can be lost; upload-pending items vanish.
sharepoint_cache.before_cleaning: Use Office Upload Center / Office settings instead
sharepoint_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the Office cache can hold pending uploads. Description ('Known folder mask') is wrong.

sharepoint_desktop_cache.used_for: Office's local document cache with pending uploads.
sharepoint_desktop_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right; duplicate of 'sharepoint_cache'. Description ('SharePoint Designer workflow cache') is wrong.

stripe_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\stripe may hold the Stripe CLI config with API keys.
stripe_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

supabase_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Supabase holds CLI auth and local state.
supabase_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

tailscale_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Tailscale is the per-user Tailscale data folder (GUI state, logs, possibly node identity).
tailscale_cache.used_for: Deletion can force re-login of the device to the tailnet.
tailscale_cache.risk: Device may leave the tailnet / need re-authentication.
tailscale_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

tresorit_cache.what: Tresorit's cache and logs. Tresorit documents its logs at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tresorit\v0.8\Logs, not under %APPDATA%.
tresorit_cache.used_for: Logs are diagnostics (may contain file names); the cache is rebuilt.
tresorit_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics; little else for logs.
tresorit_cache.catalog_concern: Paths are under Roaming (%APPDATA%) but Tresorit documents Local\Tresorit\v0.8; this likely finds nothing.

vercel_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\vercel (com.vercel.cli) holds the CLI auth token and config.
vercel_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

virtualbox_cache.what: %APPDATA%\VirtualBox (VirtualBox.xml machine registry) and %USERPROFILE%\VirtualBox VMs (the virtual machines themselves: disk images, snapshots, settings, logs).
virtualbox_cache.used_for: This is where VirtualBox stores your VMs by default. Nothing here is rebuilt.
virtualbox_cache.risk: Permanent loss of virtual machines and everything inside them.
virtualbox_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right - this is user data, not a cache.

wg_easy_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor (wg-easy is normally a server/Docker tool). Would hold WireGuard peer configs/keys.
wg_easy_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

windows_sandbox_cache.what: Not documented by Microsoft. LocalState of the Windows Sandbox app package (app state). The sandbox itself discards its contents on close.
windows_sandbox_cache.used_for: App state for Windows Sandbox; the sandbox environment is rebuilt each launch anyway.
windows_sandbox_cache.risk: Unknown; may reset the Sandbox app or break it until repaired. Little space to gain.
windows_sandbox_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: an undocumented package LocalState, not a cache.

wireguard_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. WireGuard for Windows stores tunnel configs (with private keys) - normally under Program Files\WireGuard\Data; these per-user folders are not documented.
wireguard_cache.risk: Lost tunnels and private keys if present.
wireguard_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

box_logs.what: Box Drive's own log files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Box\Box\logs, one of the folders Box lists for collecting Box Drive logs by hand.
box_logs.used_for: Troubleshooting: Box Product Support may ask for these logs (Help > Send Logs) when you file a case about a Box Drive error.
box_logs.risk: You lose the history you would send to Box support for a past problem. Files, the sync database (Box\Box\data) and unsynced files are in other folders and are not touched.
box_logs.before_cleaning: If you have an open Box support case, send the logs first (Box Drive > gear > Help > Send Logs).

google_drive_logs.what: Google Drive for desktop (DriveFS) log files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\DriveFS\Logs. Google's support article has you zip exactly this Logs folder to send to support.
google_drive_logs.used_for: Diagnosing sync, sign-in and sign-out problems. Google prefers Settings > Generate Diagnostic Info, but the folder is used when the app will not open.
google_drive_logs.risk: Past diagnostic history is lost. Your Drive files and the local content cache are elsewhere under DriveFS and are not touched.
google_drive_logs.before_cleaning: If you are working with Google support on a Drive problem, collect the logs first.
google_drive_logs.catalog_concern: The label still names Backup and Sync, which Google replaced with Drive for desktop; only the DriveFS Logs folder is targeted.

pcloud_logs.what: Diagnostic logs in the catalog's pCloud Logs folder. pCloud support asks for Drive logs when investigating sync failures, but its public article does not confirm this Windows folder path.
pcloud_logs.used_for: Troubleshooting sync problems with pCloud support. The app does not need old logs to run.
pcloud_logs.risk: Past diagnostic history is lost. Only the Logs folder is targeted, never the pCloud Drive cache or settings beside it.
pcloud_logs.before_cleaning: Close pCloud Drive if you want every log removed; files it holds open are skipped.
pcloud_logs.catalog_concern: Vendor documentation confirms the support purpose, not the exact path. Keep this limited to Logs; never widen to the pCloud profile, cache or upload staging.
